title: A fused cell-reference parse and one ampersand probe per part cut the XLSX fact builder; the stylesheet parse stops copying every event; carrying facts across a snapshot chain is rejected as unreachable
decision: retained, implemented in litchi-xlsx, with the snapshot-chain part rejected and kept as a patch
code_state: crates/litchi-xlsx only; no public API, error type, limit or output byte changed; no new unsafe and no new dependency
reason_codes: change 0622 named its own successor: 'the next reduction on this route is the builder's per-cell r parse and per-element ampersand probe, not the writer'. Both are removed, and the builder falls about 40% while admitting and declining exactly the same worksheets

every replaced test is provably the same test: the fused reference parsers are compared against parse_a1 and parse_one_based_row over 484 byte strings covering every branch of both, the whole-part ampersand probe is the same predicate as the per-tag probe, and the two redundant name comparisons were comparisons of a value with itself

XLSX-5 is answered without moving a refusal: styles::parse already retains only a count, so what the survey measured is the traversal; removing its per-event Event::into_owned and NamespaceResolver clone removes exactly 80 allocation calls and 6,457 allocated bytes per planning with the same events, checks and messages

substituting the existing styles::stream_count for styles::parse is declined and frozen as a design: process_ooxml short-circuits on MCE-free input, so parse never runs the MCE validator while stream_count always does, and the two disagree on trailing text, DTDs, processing instructions, custom entities, a late declaration, unbound prefixes, depth, event count and several stream-only bounds; the error type and message would move as well

carrying facts across a snapshot chain is implemented, tested with change 0622's oracle extended to chains, and then rejected: no public API seeds a value-only edit from a post-commit snapshot, so the capture is paid on every commit and read on none, at a measured 0.07-1.78% of a whole save

value identity is proved two ways: 34 of 34 (case, shape) published-package sha256 pairs are identical, and change 0622's differential oracle reports the same funnel and the same 2,790 comparisons as it did before the change

accepted_evidence.counts: callgrind isolation pairs, N=1 and N=11, differenced and divided by 10, three legs (before, after, after-with-chain) over one_edit_save on medium/dense-sparse/noncompact, one_percent_edit_save on medium/dense-sparse, managed one_edit_save on medium and the 0601 producer-shaped edit selectors; whole-iteration totals plus per-symbol inclusive Ir
accepted_evidence.allocations: litchi-perf-baseline-alloc with the change-0538 phase regions, five samples per leg, maximum per region, two cases over three shapes
accepted_evidence.timing: tools/perf-baseline, --warmup 5 --samples 30, order A1 B1 B2 A2 on CPU 11, followed by four before-only runs F1..F4 for the A/A floor in the same window, over five source-backed cell-value cases and three shapes plus the two producer-shaped edit selectors
accepted_evidence.value_identity: output_sha256 for 34 (case, shape) pairs across eight source-backed edit cases, four shapes including vendor-extension, and the two producer-shaped edit selectors
accepted_evidence.differential_oracle: change 0622's oracle unchanged (five tests, 2,790 corpus comparisons, same funnel), plus LITCHI_0622_FULL_ORACLE=1 in release, plus two new change-0635 tests comparing the fused reference parsers against the shared ones over 484 byte strings
accepted_evidence.chain_rejection: the rejected part measured as its own leg against the retained change, plus a reachability analysis of every public entry point that could seed a second commit

accepted_costs.instruction_counts: instructions rank work, not latency; callgrind counts rep movsb per byte and runs SHA-256 in software; one deterministic run per leg
accepted_costs.effect_below_floor: the whole-iteration effect is well under this host's A/A floor, so the paired timing bounds rather than confirms it and the counts carry the result
accepted_costs.styles_scale: the harness stylesheet is 603 bytes and 26 events, so XLSX-5's instruction saving is inside the symbol's own run-to-run variation; only its allocation saving is exact. A larger, MCE-bearing Excel stylesheet would save proportionally more, and that case is modelled, not measured
accepted_costs.debug_assert: raw_attribute's colon-free precondition is pinned by debug_assert! in debug builds only; in release it rests on the four literal call sites

known_gaps.real_producer_reach: unchanged from change 0622: of 391 real worksheet parts under test-data/, 207 are admitted to the shared traversal, exactly one is accepted by the value-only planning validator, and that one publishes facts; change 0602 established the editor admits none of the 95 real .xlsx fixtures
known_gaps.second_commit: still open, and now measured: a snapshot derived from a rewrite drops its facts, and closing that gap costs 0.07-1.78% of a save for a benefit no public caller can reach. The implementation and its oracle are retained as patch/0635-chain-facts.patch
known_gaps.stream_count: raw::styles::stream_count is not refusal-equivalent to raw::styles::parse; substituting it is frozen as a design and not implemented
known_gaps.formulas: worksheets carrying <f> are still declined by design, not by measurement
known_gaps.styles_on_real_files: no corpus in this repository reaches capture_auxiliary_source with a stylesheet that carries the markup-compatibility namespace, so the full tokenising MCE path is unmeasured

withheld: any registered speedup, throughput, cold-cache, physical-I/O, range-source, concurrency-scaling, real-producer or cross-platform result

provenance.host: AMD EPYC 9R45, 32 cores, 123 GiB, Linux 7.0.0-1012-aws, rustc 1.95.0, valgrind 3.26.0
